extracted.intended_audience: students and teachers of American literature (undergraduate/graduate), literary critics and readers studying early-20th-century American authors and poets
extracted.subtask_description: Reading-and-study guidance for evaluating and teaching works by early-20th-century American authors and poets, offering questions on form, influence, themes, and artistic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect the unexpected / sincerity vs posedness (Kreymborg)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Kreymborg is a rebel against all conventions of form and content in poetry; consequently, the one thing to be expected in his work is the unexpected. How far his utterances are sincere and how far posed, each reader must judge for himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the work for genuineness versus affected pose; be open to unconventional forms and content as an expected attribute of the poet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess authorial spirit and tone (Kreymborg)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the quoted characterization ('An insinuating, meddlesome, quizzical, inquiring spirit; sometimes a clown, oftener a wit, now and then a lyric poet...') as a starting-point in discussing Mr. Kreymborg's qualities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze tone, persona, and multifaceted voice — e.g., wit, clownishness, lyricism — and how these traits shape the poems; compare actual texts against this descriptive sketch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situate verse within contemporary art movements (Kreymborg)
rubrics_metrics.description: The new movements in art--Futurist, Cubist, Vorticist--should be remembered in studying Mr. Kreymborg's verse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider influence and parallels with contemporary visual/avant-garde movements when interpreting form, fragmentation, imagery, and experiment in the poetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy in words (Kreymborg)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is to be said of his economy in words?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate concision and the poet's use (or sparing use) of language; assess whether brevity enhances or undermines effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realism vs caricature vs artistic portraiture (Sinclair Lewis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you recognize Gopher Prairie as a type? Is Mr. Lewis's picture photography, caricature, or the kind of portraiture that is art? Or to what degree do you find all these elements?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine the balance between documentary realism, satirical exaggeration, and artistic shaping in the depiction of place/people; give examples from the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary interest of the work (story, characterization, satire, propaganda) (Sinclair Lewis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the main interest of the book in the story? in the characterization? in the satire? or in an element of propaganda?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify which element dominates and analyze how authorial choices (plot structure, characterization, tone, polemic devices) serve that primary interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate embedded ideological/constructive theories (Sinclair Lewis)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is to be said of the constructive theory of living proposed by the heroine? Is it better or worse than the standard that prevailed before she went to Gopher Prairie to live?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine explicit or implicit social/ethical proposals within the work and compare them to prevailing norms; assess persuasiveness and literary integration of the ideology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain success, permanence, and defects (Sinclair Lewis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the success of the book. What, if any, elements of permanent value do you find? What conspicuous defects?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze factors behind the work's contemporary success and appraise which qualities may endure or prove ephemeral; note major weaknesses with textual evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read background prose and related works for context (Vachel Lindsay)
rubrics_metrics.description: Read for background A Handy Guide for Beggars and Adventures while Preaching the Gospel of Beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the author's prose and explanatory texts to inform interpretation of the poems and performance practice; background reading contextualizes themes and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess performability and musical element in poetry (Vachel Lindsay)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lindsay presents his poems as experiments aiming to restore a vaudeville/Greek half-chanted lyric where one-third of music must be added by the instinct of the reader; big general contrasts between main sections should be the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read poems aloud; attend to cadence, suggested melody, contrasts, and printed cues (italics, capitals, spacing); judge the poem's performative demands and how performance affects meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of typographical and notational aids for expression (Vachel Lindsay)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Lindsay often prints aids to expression by means of italics, capitals, spaces, and even side notes and other notes on expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how typographical marks and editorial notations guide oral delivery and interpretive choices; treat them as part of the poem's expressive apparatus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter selection and imaginative range (Vachel Lindsay)
rubrics_metrics.description: What different kinds of material appeal especially to Mr. Lindsay's imagination? How do you explain his choice, and his limitations?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catalog recurring themes and subjects; assess whether they demonstrate breadth or limitation and theorize reasons (biographical, ideological, aesthetic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate ethical/missionary impulse versus aesthetic/singing element (Vachel Lindsay)
rubrics_metrics.description: What effect upon his poetry has the missionary spirit which is so strong in him? Is his poetry more valuable for its singing element or for its ethical appeal? Do you discover any special originality?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh the moral/evangelical tendencies against musical/lyric qualities; determine which gives the poems their primary value and whether originality emerges from the combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare use of local material with contemporaries (Vachel Lindsay)
rubrics_metrics.description: How does his use of local material compare with that of Masters? of Frost? of Sandburg?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform comparative analysis of place-based imagery and regional focus across authors, noting differences in scope, tone, and function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze rhythmic sense and formal devices (Vachel Lindsay)
rubrics_metrics.description: Study his rhythmic sense in different poems, the verse forms that he uses, the tendencies in rhyme, his use of refrain, of onomatopoeia, of catalogues, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Close-read prosodic elements: meter, rhythm, rhyme schemes, refrains, sound devices and their contribution to meaning and performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address objectionable elements and defenses (Vachel Lindsay)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does Mr. Lindsay offend your poetic taste? If so, can you justify his use of the material you object to?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If elements provoke negative reaction, identify literary or contextual justifications (performance, mission, innovation) and argue for or against their legitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate future promise and development (Vachel Lindsay)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you judge that Mr. Lindsay is likely to write much greater poetry than he has hitherto produced?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess trajectories in craft, ambition, originality, and public reception to speculate about future achievements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare cross-medium output (drawings vs poems) (Vachel Lindsay)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Lindsay's drawings are worth study for comparison with his poems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze thematic and stylistic correspondences between visual art and poetry to enrich interpretation of imagery, composition, and aesthetic aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare development of poetic forms across poets (Vachel Lindsay)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare Mr. Lindsay's development of the idea of the 'poem game' with the 'poem dance' of Bliss Carman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cross-author formal comparison to trace genealogies of particular experimental forms and their functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider poet's social role and impact (Vachel Lindsay)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider Mr. Lindsay as the 'poet of democracy.' What is he likely to do for the people? for poetry?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate civic aspirations and accessibility of work; assess potential cultural influence and place in popular vs elite poetic traditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read authors' critical writings to understand practice (Amy Lowell)
rubrics_metrics.description: As Miss Lowell is the principal exponent of the theories of imagism and free verse in this country, careful reading of some of her critical papers leads to a better understanding of her work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the author's essays, prefaces, and critical studies to grasp theoretical commitments that inform poetic practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare effectiveness of metrical vs free-verse methods (Amy Lowell)
rubrics_metrics.description: In judging her work, consider separately her poems in regular metrical form and those in free verse. Decide which method is better suited to her type of imagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate individual poems by form, asking whether meter or free verse more successfully realizes the poet's aims and imaginative temperament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trace cultural sources of inspiration (Amy Lowell)
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent does her inspiration come from cultural sources--travel, literature, art, music?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and assess influences from travel and other arts; examine how these sources shape imagery, themes, and technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine imagery: origin, sensory detail, and influences (Amy Lowell)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider especially her presentation of 'images.' How far do these seem to be derived from direct experience? Test them by your own experience. What principles seem to determine her choice of details? Which sense impressions--sight, sound, taste, smell, touch--does she most frequently and successfully suggest? Note instances where her figures of speech sharpen the imagery and others where they seem to distort it. In what ways is the influence of Keats perceptible in her work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform sensory inventory and source-checks; assess fidelity to experience and metaphorical shaping; trace intertextual influences (e.g., Keats).

rubrics_metrics.name: Study historical imagery in specific collections (Amy Lowell)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is worth while to make special study of the historical imagery of the poems in Can Grande's Castle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focused analysis of a single volume's use of historical reference and its interpretive function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analogize to impressionistic painting (Amy Lowell)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are familiar with the impressionistic method of painting, work out an analogy between it and Miss Lowell's word pictures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cross-art analogy to elucidate compositional techniques: fragmentary detail, coloristic imagery, focus on perception rather than narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate study of free verse and polyphonic prose; form-content fit (Amy Lowell)
rubrics_metrics.description: Study separately her varieties of free verse and polyphonic prose (cf. her study of Paul Fort and the preface to Can Grande's Castle). Choose several poems in which you think the free verse form is especially adapted to the content and draw conclusions as to the problems of development of this kind of verse or of its possible influence upon regular metrical forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare genres/forms within the author's oeuvre for suitability to themes and to trace possible influence on broader poetic practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use exemplar poem as evaluative basis (Amy Lowell)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the following poem by Miss Lowell as a basis for judging her work: FRAGMENT (poem).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply close analysis of a representative poem as a test case for general claims about the poet's style and strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess chronological development and distinguishing qualities (Amy Lowell)
rubrics_metrics.description: In summing up Miss Lowell's achievement, consider the different phases of it that appear in her volumes taken in chronological order, noting the successive influences under which she has come. In what qualities does she stand out strikingly from other contemporary poets? Do you expect different and more important work from her in the future?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do a diachronic study of volumes, map changing influences and salient distinguishing qualities, and forecast future development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read poems aloud to capture full lyric effect (Edna St. Vincent Millay)
rubrics_metrics.description: The poems need to be read aloud to give the full effect of their passion and lyric beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oral reading is essential for assessing emotional intensity, meter, and musicality; judge the poems' auditory power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare naïveté and philosophical depth (Edna St. Vincent Millay)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare Miss Millay's naïveté with that of Blake. Do you find suggestions of philosophy behind it or sheer emotion?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze whether apparent simplicity masks philosophical complexity or remains primarily emotional; use comparative exemplars (e.g., Blake).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate later work for growth vs sophistication (Edna St. Vincent Millay)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does Miss Millay's later work show growth toward greatness or toward sophisticated cleverness?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess trajectory in craft and substance across early and later poems to judge whether development is substantive or merely mannered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start with key canonical work and test sources and merits (Edgar Lee Masters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with The Spoon River Anthology. How much does it owe to its model? to other literary sources? to the central Illinois environment in which the author grew up? What are its most conspicuous merits and defects? How do you explain each?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the major work as focal point to trace models, local influences, and to enumerate and explain strengths and weaknesses with textual evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test verisimilitude and universality of sketches (Edgar Lee Masters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Test the sketches by your own experience of small town life. Which seem truest to individual character and most universal in type?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare textual portrayals to observed reality and judge which pieces achieve individual specificity versus universal archetype.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare with contemporaries for influence and contrast (Edgar Lee Masters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare similar sketches of personalities by Edwin Arlington Robinson, which Mr. Masters had not read until after his book was published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use contemporaneous works for comparative analysis to isolate convergent or divergent techniques and independent invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess success in achieving stated artistic/social aims (Edgar Lee Masters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider how far Mr. Masters has achieved his avowed purpose 'to analyze society, to satirise society, to tell a story, to expose the machinery of life, to present a working model of the big world'; to create beauty, and to depict 'our sorrows and hopes...'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the text against its declared objectives across social analysis, satire, narrative clarity, and aesthetic creation; cite passages that fulfill or fail those aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain popularity and chances of canonicity (Edgar Lee Masters)
rubrics_metrics.description: How do you explain the sudden popularity of the Anthology? What are its chances of becoming a classic?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze cultural, stylistic, and thematic reasons for popularity and judge the work's durability and likelihood of entering the canon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare later volumes to early landmark for development (Edgar Lee Masters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Read one of Mr. Masters' later volumes and compare it with the Anthology as to merits and defects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform diachronic comparison to chart development, shifts in technique, and recurring weaknesses or improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trace literary influences (Edgar Lee Masters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Masters has always been a great reader. Trace, as far as you can, the influence of the following authors: Homer; the Bible; Poe; Keats; Shelley; Swinburne; Browning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify echoes, thematic parallels, and formal borrowings from named antecedents; show specific textual correspondences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draw parallels with contemporaries (Edgar Lee Masters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Draw parallels between his work and the work of (1) Edwin Arlington Robinson, (2) Robert Frost, (3) Vachel Lindsay, and (4) Carl Sandburg.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map stylistic, thematic, and formal affinities and differences to situate the author within his literary milieu.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study effect of professional background on poetry (Edgar Lee Masters)
rubrics_metrics.description: An interesting study might be made of the effects of Mr. Masters' legal training upon his poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine how legal training may shape approach to voice, testimony, social analysis, procedural perspective, or diction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare genre success (poet vs novelist) via specific works (Edgar Lee Masters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare Children of the Market Place with the Anthology or Domesday Book. Is Mr. Masters more successful as poet or as novelist?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cross-genre comparison to assess strengths and limitations in different literary forms and determine relative success.
